Panels and casts of statues-stele accompany the visit; the exhibition curated by Enrico Giannicedda (inaugurated in October 2023) exhibits finds of almost six thousand years, including statues-stele, urns, Roman crockery, medieval weapons, coins and keys. Show available by reservation.
3g2p42.38: Six thousand years of Lunigiana in a hall.
1bmq6g2.161: Small village entirely in stone, among the best preserved medieval centers of the area, with squares, courtyards, alleys, numerous covered passages and tower houses.
6yv4ll.95: Borgo on the right of the homonymous stream, also known for the houses-towers and covered passages.
2q0kl8.348: Medieval village at the crossroads between the Bagnone valley and the Magra valley, ancient free-of-duty villa and crossed by the Via Francigena, with the ruins of Malnido dei Malaspina castle and the Ethnographic Museum of Lunigiana in a mill of the sixteenth century; in the territory the villages of Filetto, with its forest of chestnut trees, Virgoletta and Malgrate.
18y950w.681: In a mill of the community of the sixteenth century, remained in operation until the 1930s, on the outskirts of the village along the Via Francigena; the original water wheels, moved by the nearby stream Bagnone, are still in place. Founded in 1977 by the Cultural Association Manfredo Giuliani, it exhibits three millstones of different stones (a sandstone for chestnuts, blue stone for corn, basalt for wheat), objects of chestnut processing, breeding, cheese, fishing and handicrafts, amulets of fertility, the "Raganelle" of the Holy Week, cradles in beech including the famous cradle of Bratto, a rebuilt Lunigiana cuisine and a large frame.
qeu7qc.65: The peasant life of Lunigiana inside a real watermill.
xlzvvg.447: The remains of the 12th century castle stand on a rocky spur overlooking the road and the ford on the Magra; it was the seat of the Malaspina of Spino Secco, which in the division of assets of 1221 held Villafranca for its commercial and financial advantages. Next are the remains of the church of San Nicolò and the square dedicated to Dante, guest of the Malaspina; from the area of the castle the medieval road leads to the parish church of San Giovanni.
1eltcms.57: The medieval heart of the "vina franca" on Francigena.
15kbis8.697: The name derives from the Greek . ...Fulacterion , fortified village: born as a Byzantine fortification between the 5th and 6th centuries, it preserves the quadrangular plan of the late antique castra with perpendicular streets and central squares, still closed by the walls of the 17th century. In 1351 it was a market village on the Via Francigena, in the feud of Malgrate; in the seventeenth century it passed to the Ariberti of Cremona, which extended it with a wide central street, a square and a palace (the Borgo degli Ariberti) next to the church of Saints Jacopo and Antonio and the convent of the Fatebenefratelli, connected by suspended bridges and arches above the doors. In the ancient core narrow alleys, the Jewish Village and a large market square.
g12wl2.52: A late antique village-fortress remained almost intact.
1uy0fyi.469: Just outside the walls of Filetto, a centuries-old chestnut grove surrounds the small oratory of San Genesio, still a goal of devotion; Carlo Caselli called him "Selva of suicides." Here were found eleven stele statues, today at the Museum of the Stone Statues of Pontremoli, and two menhirs are still standing. Around 25 August, from the 17th century, there is the fair of San Genesio, once a cattle market and today a festival with music and products from Lunigiana under chestnut trees.
1k1ky16.62: Secular chestnuts and menhirs where the stele statues have re-emerged.
17ucz9c.221: Village of road lying on the ridge of a hill, with walls more than ten meters high, fountains, numerous speaking doors, the Malaspina castle and the church of Santi Gervasio and Protasio, whose bell tower dominates the village.

1scj7rl.57: A watchtower on the gate of the Bagnone valley.
